site.title: Planet Tracker
intro: Planet Tracker is a web application that explores the eight planets and their moons in our Solar System. The larger images on this page are used intentionally to reflect the enormous scale of space. Astronomy deals with distances so great that they are difficult to imagine, so the visuals are given more room in order to better convey the size of the Solar System, the Milky Way galaxy, and the wider observable universe. Users can also contribute to the application by adding their own moons. Each moon can include a name, the planet it orbits, and other details including an image, allowing the collection to grow over time. This makes the app interactive and continually expanding, giving users the opportunity to build their own catalogue of moons and explore how different worlds relate to one another.

vastness.heading: Understanding the Vast Scale of Space
paragraphs: The Solar System may seem enormous to us, but in the context of the universe it is incredibly small. One way to understand this scale is through comparison. If the entire Solar System were reduced to the size of a tennis ball, our Milky Way galaxy would be roughly the size of North America.

The galaxy contains hundreds of billions of stars, many with their own planetary systems. Our Solar System is located in one of the spiral arms of the Milky Way galaxy, far from its centre. The Milky Way is about 100,000 light-years across and is just one of billions of galaxies in the observable universe. When we look up at the night sky, we are seeing only a tiny fraction of what exists.

scaleStory.title: The Observable Universe
scaleStory.caption:
An illustration of the observable universe. Our galaxy is a tiny part of a vast cosmic structure.

Fun fact...ish: At 100 mph, it would take about 300 trillion years to reach the edge of the observable universe. You’d need roughly 1 sextillion litres of petrol, costing around €2 sextillion. Even if every human who has ever lived was born one after another and took turns driving, we would still need another 3.5 trillion people to finish the journey.

scaleStory.title: The Milky Way
scaleStory.caption:
The Milky Way is a barred spiral galaxy about 100,000 light-years across. Our Solar System is located on a spiral arm. It is marked in yellow.

Fun fact...ish: Driving at 100 mph, it would take around 70 billion years to cross the galaxy. You’d need about 200 quadrillion litres of petrol, costing roughly €360 quadrillion — far more fuel than exists on Earth. So don't forget your cridit card!

scaleStory.title: Our Solar System
scaleStory.caption:
Our Solar System contains eight planets orbiting the Sun. This app tracks the planets and key facts about each one.

Fun fact...ish: At 100 mph, it would take over 60 million years to drive from one side of the Solar System to the other. You’d need roughly 200 trillion litres of petrol, costing around €350 trillion.

scaleStory.title: Earth
scaleStory.caption:
Earth is our home, our only home, a small but extraordinary world in the vastness of space.

Fun fact...ish: Driving around the Earth at 100 km/h would take over 16 days non-stop. You’d burn around 3,000 litres of petrol, costing roughly €5,000 — all just to circle one tiny planet in a vast universe.
